statements.text: Epithelioid sarcoma is a rare cancerous tumor.
Epithelioid sarcoma is characterized by loss of SMARCB1/INI1 (integrase interactor 1) or other proteins of the SWI/SNF complex.
Epithelioid sarcoma usually begins as a painless, firm growth or bump that may be accompanied by an open wound (ulceration) in the skin covering the growth.
Epithelioid sarcoma is known for aggressive behavior, including a high recurrence rate and regional lymph node metastases.
Epithelioid sarcoma most often occurs in the soft tissue of the fingers, hands and forearms of young adults, with a peak incidence at 35 years of age.
Two distinct types of epithelioid sarcoma, proximal and distal, are distinguished with varying biology and treatment outcomes.
Among staged patients with epithelioid sarcoma, lymph node metastasis occurs in approximately 17.5% of cases.
Locoregional recurrence within the ipsilateral limb occurs in 27% of epithelioid sarcoma patients at a median time of 56 months post-primary treatment.
Distant metastases in epithelioid sarcoma develop in 21% of patients, with all occurring in the chest.
At presentation, 31% of epithelioid sarcoma patients had metastases, the majority of which were lymph node metastases identified on radionuclide imaging with PET CT.
Epithelioid sarcoma is diagnosed by clinical examination and by testing a small sample of the tumor (biopsy) in a laboratory.
Neo-adjuvant or adjuvant radiotherapy may be recommended for epithelioid sarcoma, as it reduces the local recurrence rate.
Sentinel lymph node biopsy should be considered in epithelioid sarcoma patients.
Doxorubicin-based regimens are recommended for advanced epithelioid sarcoma.

Tazemetostat, an EZH2 methyltransferase inhibitor, has shown promising results in epithelioid sarcoma patients and was approved by the FDA in 2020 for use in patients with advanced epithelioid sarcoma.
Novel therapies, including immunotherapy, are still being investigated for epithelioid sarcoma.
A prospective Italian observational study aimed to provide a description of the population affected by epithelioid sarcoma.
Clinical trials are evaluating immunotherapy combinations and novel agents for epithelioid sarcoma, including pembrolizumab and ONO-4538HSC.
